messages.subject: Re: Error in sequenza.extract: Missing values are not allowed in logR input
messages.subject_clean: Error in sequenza.extract: Missing values are not allowed in logR input
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

  So from this I have started working towards my own loop through the chromosomes and catching those that experience any error. To this end, do you happen to have any method for concatenating the output of sequenza extract I am not seeing built in? It appears to be returning a list of lists of lists?

If I had:
chr1 <- sequenza.extract(…, chromosome.list = "1")

chr2 <- sequenza.extract(…, chromosome.list = "2")

How could I combine them in a way sequenza likes, as if I ran sequenza.extract(…, chromosome.list = c("2","3"))

Thanks you.

-Brad

On Friday, May 25, 2018 at 5:27:17 AM UTC-4, Francesco Favero wrote:
> It may not be optimal, but you could skip chromosome 17 for that sample:
>
> sequenza.extract(…, chromosome.list = c(1:16,18:22, "X", "Y”))
>
> I think the problem is the segmentation: if for any reason you know already the segments for that sample you may try to run the function with
>
> sequenza.extract(…, breaks = breakpoints_you_know_already)
>
> if you don’t have breakpoints and you really want chromosome 17 (well, there are a couple of important genes there after all :P), you may try as follow:
>
> 1) run sequenza.extract as I suggested excluding chr 17
> 2) from the segmentation results, take the first 3 columns: chromosome, start, end and save in a object/file (name the columns chrom, start.pos, end.pos)
> 3) open the file/object and manually add a line for chromosome 17 (eg from start to end of the chromosome)
> 4) run sequenza extract with the modified breakpoints
> 5) visual inspect chromosome 17 in the results: if there are other clear breakpoints, you should manually modify the breaks file again and return to point 4
>
> I hope this is not too convoluted, I know it’s very annoying to deal manually with such matters.
>
> Please let me know if you have success in the process!
>
> Francesco
>
>

messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

    I am having difficulty troubleshooting an error running extract. For now it appears to happen in a single sample for chromosomes 1 and 8.

Processing 1: Error in if (c > b) m <- if (a <= c) a else c :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
Error in if (!is.null(breaks) & nrow(breaks) > 0) { :
  argument is of length zero

A fresh copy of the input data did not resolve anything. I tried looking over the input lines and did not see anything that struck me as 'missing', but Im not certain what I should be looking for. Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

-bwubb

messages.subject: Change repository team name for sequenza

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I've changed the sequenza_tools team name in sequenzatool, so now sequenza git repository is located at https://bitbucket.org/sequenzatools/sequenza

This change is due to the fact that I couldn't set up a repository web page with the "_" character in the team name.
As a result, now we also have a main page associated with the development team :)

https://sequenzatools.bitbucket.io

I hope this is not causing too much inconveniences.

Best regards

Francesco

Sorry for the slow reply.

Have you tried the new version in bitbucket.
I remember this error from some other user, and I think we may have fixed it.

install with:
    library(devtools)
    install_bitbucket("sequenzatools/sequenza@cleanup")

The new version is stable, and im my opition is much better then 2.1.2 (currently on CRAN).
It is lacking documentation for some functions (but the old docs are still valid, I just wanted to rewrite some of them)

Best

Francesco
